pagerduty-bot: [PAGERDUTY] Page fired — service: redis-main — urgency: high — alert: redis-accept-queue > 90% (us-east-1). Incident: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PD12345 :rotating_light:

ops-bot: automated-detect: accept_queue rise detected across redis-main pods (avg accept_queue=880/1000, client_count ~10.2k, maxclients=10000). Elevated latency and connection rejects reported. Collecting metrics...

ops-bot: logs snapshot:
```
# redis-cli INFO clients
connected_clients:10212
client_longest_output_list:0
client_biggest_input_buf:0
blocked_clients:34
```

sara-oncall: @pagerduty-bot acked. I'm on it, incoming triage. :hand:

sara-oncall: quick summary — app 503s and timeouts showing from 12:18 UTC, spikes correlate with a rollout spike + increased traffic from background job. Not seeing a recent config change to redis itself. Pushing telemetry to datadog.

dan-sre: I see connection errors in frontend logs too, sample: `ERR redis: connection refused (dial tcp ...)` — pgbouncer pools showing saturation.

mike-dev: app logs (cut):
```
2026-03-15T12:20:02Z GET /predict 504 upstream timeout redis
2026-03-15T12:20:08Z POST /embed 503 redis dial tcp: i/o timeout
```

kevin-db: tagging in. Initial thought: client_count > maxclients -> new connections rejected. Could be slow clients holding connections (blocked_clients=34 suggests some blocked I/O). Check slowlog and AOF rewrite? Any RDB persistence job running?

ops-bot: slowlog top entries (trimmed):
```
# id=2345 time=1678873200 microsecs=412345 cmd=GET key=user:346 profile:heavy
# id=2349 time=1678873220 microsecs=389001 cmd=LPUSH key=job_queue
```

kevin-db: mitigation plan: 1) Open temporary read-only routing for non-critical endpoints 2) Add a replica (scale redis-replica) 3) Tune pgbouncer/connection pooling to reduce per-client connections 4) If needed enable fallback cache miss throttling in gateway. I'll run step 2 now.

kevin-db: running: `kubectl scale deployment redis-replica -n prod --replicas=3` -> pending pods creating.

ops-bot: k8s events: redis-replica-2 creating, redis-replica-3 creating.

mike-dev: can we gate background job traffic? It's definitely contributing.

sara-oncall: I've paused the scheduled background worker rollout in the job service and set concurrency=1 for the job queue. That should reduce new connections over next 30s. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: traffic routing change applied: /metrics and /admin routed to replica-read only pool. Non-critical read endpoints have 60% traffic routed away from primary.

olivia-csm: any customer-facing impact? I need a short blurb for Slack status and to send to CS.

kevin-db: current impact: intermittent 503/504 on feature endpoints that hit cache. Non-critical reads mostly unaffected after routing change. Estimated affected users ~0.8% of requests in us-east-1 over last 5m.

kevin-db: if replica spin-up completes and connection pooling reduces pressure we should stabilize. Monitoring: accept_queue and rejected_connections.

ops-bot: redis-replica pods are Ready. Rebalance in progress.

dan-sre: I bumped pgbouncer max_client_conn on poolers from 12000 -> 18000 to allow graceful draining (config change rolled to 3 poolers). Watch for mem pressure.

kevin-db: running a short TTL flush on some large keys to free memory and reduce swap risk: `redis-cli --rdb` (snapshot) then `EVAL ...` (targeted cleanup).

ops-bot: metrics: accept_queue dropped to 25% average across primaries. client_count down to ~6300. Rejected connections near zero. Latency 95p reduced from 420ms -> 120ms.

mike-dev: seeing 200s again for most requests, thanks. Confirmed job backoff reduced traffic.

olivia-csm: ok — drafting customer note: "Intermittent caching errors in us-east-1 due to backend connection saturation. We mitigated by temporarily routing traffic, scaling replicas, and tuning pooling; most customers restored. Engineering investigating root cause and will follow up." Want sign-off?

sara-oncall: sign-off. Add timeline and next steps.

kevin-db: next steps: run postmortem, check persistent causes (slow commands, memory pressure, job fanout), consider circuit-breaker for job spikes, add alert for accept_queue > 80% plus slowlog rate > threshold.

dan-sre: handing off to kevin-db for DB oncall for deeper root cause analysis — I need to rotate off for next shift. All mitigation notes in ops runbook.

kevin-db: acked, taking over. I'll update PD incident with root-cause progress and put a follow-up postmortem ticket.

ops-bot: [INCIDENT] status -> mitigated. PD: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PD12345/status

kevin-db: final note for handoff: accepted actions: scale replicas, pgbouncer bump, paused jobs. Persisted action items: analyze slow commands, review persistence config, and add rate-limit protections on job producers. Leaving monitoring watch for 2 hours. Handoff to night oncall @dan-sre (FYI).

olivia-csm: thank you all — will send brief to CS and keep customers updated if anything changes. :pray:

sara-oncall: closing this thread for now. If anything regresses ping the PD again. :lock:
